column1: Outputs (formulas in words — build as single cells referencing the inputs)

1. Subscription pathway cost = months actually taken × your regional checkout price for one month. (There is no other honest form: a subscription has no fixed total. See ON-01, ON-02, ON-05 in Appendix A.)

2. Per-credit programme cost = per-credit-hour rate × number of credits + (number of semesters × per-semester fee). UN-01's online learning fee is verified for Fall 2026 (USD 212 under 4 credit hours; USD 531 at 4 or more — see "Verified cost bases" below). For a future term, where the fee amount may have changed, enter it as a variable (call it F), obtain the current amount from the institution's official fee page before deciding, and never let a scenario built on F present itself as a published price.

3. Rate-schedule programme cost = the sum of the actual term-by-term charges at your planned enrolment pattern. A quarterly or annual rate is never multiplied into a programme total the institution does not publish (UN-04's schedule; UN-05's annual rate).
5. Lost income = (reduction in working hours, as a fraction of full-time) × current salary × duration in years. Zero for part-time study at unchanged hours.

6. Opportunity cost = input 7 (your hourly value) × the planned study hours that are not already counted as lost income under formula 5. An hour is priced once, never twice (Chapter 7's rule): hours given up from paid work belong to formula 5; the remaining study hours belong here.
7. Total economic cost = total cash cost + lost income + opportunity cost.
8. Break-even time, per case = total economic cost ÷ that case's assumed annual gain (inputs 8, 9, 10). If a case's gain is 0, the result is Never.

9. Part-time vs full-time comparison = run the whole calculation twice (once per mode) and compare three outputs: total cash cost; total economic cost; expected completion date. Decide on the second and third outputs, as Chapter 7 instructs — the mode with the lower cash cost routinely carries the higher economic cost and the later completion.
